Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the applicant in the Court is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Shivam Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Rajeev Dhar Dwivedi, learned A.G.A. for the State-respondent and Shri Ram Krishna Yadav, learned counsel for the informant.
3.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No.743 of 2020, under Sections 406, 420 IPC, Police Station Kotwali Orai, District Jalaun,
with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that on the basis of false allegation of cheating and misappropriation, applicant has been made accused in the present matter.
5. He further submits that during investigation, applicant fully co-operated with the investigation and there is no allegation that he did not co-operate during investigation.

sentences.text: He further submits applicant is having no criminal history to his credit and all the alleged offences are triabe by Magistrate Ist Class with maximum punishment of seven years and after service of notice under Section 41-A Cr.P.C., charge-sheet has been submitted against the applicant without his arrest.

7. He further submits that applicant is having apprehension that if he will appear before the court concerned then he will be sent to jail, therefore, considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, applicant should be released on anticipatory bail.

8. Per contra, learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail and submit that apart from the present case, applicant is having criminal history of two other case of similar nature but both the counsel could not dispute the fact that in these two cases, applicant is on bail.
9.
They further could not dispute the other arguments on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
10. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. However, apart from the present case, applicant is having criminal history of two other cases of similar nature but it reflects that both these cases relate to the offences triabe by Magistrate Ist Class with maximum punishment of seven years and in both these cases, applicant is on bail.

12. Further, as far as merit of the present case is concerned, however, as per allegation, applicant misappropriated the money of the informant but offence under Sections 406, 420 IPC are triabe by Magistrate Ist Class with maximum punishment of seven years.

It also reflects, after service of notice under Section 41-A Cr.P.C., charge-sheet has been submitted against the applicant without his arrest and there is no allegation that he did not co-operate in the investigation.
13. Further, apprehension ofcustody/arrest raised by the applicant
, cannot be ruled out.

14. Further, as charge-sheet in the present matter has already been submitted, therefore, this Court finds merit in the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that custodial interrogation of the applicant in the present matter does not appear to be necessary.

15. Further, as during investigation, applicant was not arrested, therefore, there is no occasion to send him jail after submission of the charge-sheet/police report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C.
16.
Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial.
17. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application is allowed.
